claims.hypothesis: Substructure exists in the infant disk of L1527 IRS
claims.experiment: Q-band multi-epoch imaging, Gaussian fits, simulated smooth disk
claims.result: Three clumps detected consistently in independent epochs and configurations
claims.finding: Clumpy structure is physical and indicates substructure

evidence.quote: We have concluded that the clumpy structure is physical origin and are indicative of substructure in L1527 IRS.
The three clumps remain even after subtracting free-free contamination

claims.hypothesis: Clumps form a symmetric ring or spiral
claims.experiment: Compare positions, masses, 7 mm historical data
claims.result: N and S symmetric but N fainter
claims.finding: Ring/spiral plausible but individual clumps not ruled out

evidence.quote: possibilities of being independent clumps are not rules out.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Smooth disk with noise producing clumps rejected

evidence.quote: It appears that a smooth disk requires a series of coincidences to be observed as clumpy structure found in our Q-band data.

limitations_admitted.value: Masses highly uncertain due to cm dust opacity

evidence.quote: our estimated mass suffers from huge uncertainties mainly originating from poor understanding of dust opacity at cm-wavelengths.

referee_caveats_inferred: Low-S/N Q-band data with flagged long baselines
